prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts an elevated construction ledge where a vertical wall on the right (0.3 to 1.0 m away) and horizontal floor slab on the lower left (1.0 to 1.5 m away) sit in the immediate foreground, separated by wooden scaffolding poles (0.5 to 2.5 m away) from a worker standing below on lower scaffolding and a background building and street over 10 m away. Across the five frames, the camera wearer leans forward and tilts downward over the ledge as the worker below approaches upward from roughly 3.0–3.5 m away in frame 1 to about 1.5–2.0 m in frames 4 and 5, while extending his right arm to within 0.5–0.8 m of the camera. In frame 5, the camera wearer's own left hand holding a brick enters the bottom-left foreground at roughly 0.3–0.4 m, within immediate arm's reach of both the wearer and the worker's outstretched glove about 0.2 m behind it, while the worker's lower body remains occluded beneath the ledge and scaffolding throughout. The depth map clearly separates the crisscrossing foreground scaffolding poles and the worker's extended arm from the visually cluttered brick building and ground far behind them, which blend together in the RGB image. However, the map is unreliable on distant background structures over 10 m away—collapsing the opposite building, trees, and street into uniform black—and blurs depth boundaries slightly around thin ropes and between the brick and the worker's touching hand in frame 5.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the worker below the camera wearer as a single 'person' mask positioned slightly left of center in frame 1 (about 3.0–3.5 m away and below the ledge) and shifting toward the upper-center/right in frames 4 and 5 as the camera tilts down and the worker moves closer to 1.5–2.0 m. The worker's silhouette shows his torso facing upward toward the camera wearer while his lower body is occluded by the concrete ledge in frames 1–2 and by wooden scaffolding poles in frames 3–5. Across frames 3 to 5, the mask captures his right arm extending upward and to the left toward the camera wearer, coming within arm's reach (under 0.8 m) in frame 4 and meeting the camera wearer's left hand and brick (about 0.3–0.4 m away) in the bottom-left corner of frame 5. This map makes it easy to track the contiguous contour of the worker's upper body and outstretched arm against the busy bamboo scaffolding and sunlit background without visual distraction. However, it is highly unreliable for scene layout and objects: it completely misses the scaffolding, walls, metal pans, bricks in frames 1–2, a second partially visible person on the far right of frame 3 (roughly 3–4 m away), and the camera wearer's hand in frame 5, while misclassifying the held brick and hand in frame 5 as a 'hot dog' and briefly hallucinating a tiny secondary mask next to the worker in frame 2.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D yellow body keypoints and limb segments for the worker standing below the camera wearer, tracking his position from the lower-left at 3.0–3.5 m distance in frame 1 to the center and upper-right at 1.5–2.0 m distance in frames 3 through 5. The arrangement of the head, eye/ear, and shoulder keypoints shows the worker facing and looking upward toward the camera wearer across the sequence, with his torso angled beneath the ledge while his legs remain unmapped or occluded below the scaffolding. While his arms are bent near his torso (about 2.5–3.0 m away) in frames 1 and 2, the right shoulder, elbow, and wrist keypoints extend sharply downward-left in the image plane from frame 3 onward, bringing his right magenta hand skeleton in frame 4 within 0.5–0.8 m (arm's reach) of the camera wearer. The skeleton explicitly reveals the joint articulations of the worker's shoulders, elbows, and torso orientation even where dark shadows and overlapping scaffolding poles obscure his body in the RGB frames. Conversely, the pose map is unreliable in capturing full-body and multi-person geometry: it hallucinates cramped leg keypoints on the occluded lower body in frames 1 and 2, misses the worker's left forearm holding a pan in frames 4 and 5, drops the magenta hand skeleton in frame 5, and fails to detect both the camera wearer's reaching left hand in frame 5 (at 0.3–0.4 m) and the partially visible person on the right edge of frame 3.
